boundaries.evidence: Faint longitudinal line at x~123-127, clearest from S3 to S5 and readable at S2, in deep shadow (possibly yellow paint, which reads dark in shadow). The opposing approach on its left (x~12-126, lane line at x~68) has down-pointing turn arrows near S2 and S4 and a white stop bar at about y 1030 (between S4 and S5) whose right end is at x~130, so this line separates down-moving traffic from the lanes leaving upward. Above S2 the line cannot be seen; S1 continues the straight line.

In the sunlit band just above the crosswalk (near S5), sunlit asphalt (grey ~137) changes to bright concrete (~180+) at x~226-228. The crosswalk stripes end at x~213 with asphalt to x~225. Near S3 the surface colour changes at x~224-226, just right of the parked-car line. A row of four nose-to-tail vehicles (one dark car above S1, then three light cars between S1 and S4) sits at x~185-223 against this edge. Near S4, sunlit tree branches and shadow edges cross it and it is extended straight.

partial_strips: A line of parked or stopped vehicles at x~185-223 runs from above S1 to just above S4 along the kerb, with gaps of about 1.5 m. There is probably an unmarked parking strip of about 2 m inside the kerb, ending before the crosswalk at S5; no painted edge separates it from the travel lane, so no boundary is drawn.
cannot_determine: Whether x~185-226 is a parking lane or part of a single wide travel lane: no lane line is visible between e1 and the kerb.
The colour of the centre line, and its position at S1 and above S2, which are too dark to read.

Bright speckles and diagonal streaks at x~240-350 are sunlit branches of street trees over a shadowed sidewalk, not road markings. The ground there reads as sidewalk/tree area, but heavy shadow makes this a judgement call.
A thin bright diagonal line at the top-left (x~95 at the top to x~17 near S2) is a sunlit tree branch on the opposing side and was ignored.
